What is Installment Tax and does my small business have to pay it?

Installment Tax applies where your tax liability is not fully covered by PAYE and exceeds KES 40,000 for the year; it does not apply to businesses on Turnover Tax. Companies pay their estimated annual corporate tax liability in four equal installments, each due on or before the 20th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of their accounting period. What different tax obligations might a small business in Kenya have?

Depending on your activity, a business may need to register for Income Tax, Value Added Tax (VAT), Turnover Tax, Pay As You Earn (PAYE) if you employ staff, Withholding Tax, Installment Tax, Advance Tax (for commercial vehicle owners), Rental Income Tax, and Capital Gains Tax, plus you may need a Tax Compliance Certificate to prove your standing. As a sole proprietor, what's the practical difference between Turnover Tax and paying regular Income Tax on my business profit?

Turnover Tax is a flat 1.5% on gross sales with no expense deductions, filed monthly, and available to businesses turning over KES 1 million to 25 million a year. Standard Income Tax instead taxes your net profit after allowable business expenses, using the graduated individual income tax rates, and is filed annually rather than monthly. Which is more favourable depends on your margins — a low-margin, high-turnover business often pays less under TOT, while a high-margin business may prefer Income Tax's expense deductions. What are the naming rules for a limited company in Kenya?

Under the Companies Act, 2015, a private company's name must end in "Limited" or "Ltd", and a public company's must end in "plc" or "Public Limited Company". A proposed name cannot use offensive or vernacular abusive language, cannot duplicate an existing registered name without written consent, cannot match a registered trademark, and cannot contain the words "co-operative", "society", or "trade union". What is APR, and why should I check it before comparing two loan offers?

APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is the full cost of a loan expressed as a rate for a whole year, and Kenyan lenders are required to disclose it clearly to borrowers alongside any monthly or periodic rate quoted. Comparing APRs rather than just the headline monthly rate is what lets you fairly compare two loans that structure their fees differently. How do I get an M-Pesa statement for my business's bookkeeping?

You can request one through the M-Pesa app — go to M-Pesa Statements, tap See All, select Export Statements, set your date range, then Generate Statement to download it. Alternatively, dial *334#, select My Account, then M-Pesa Statement, choose the statement type and period, and enter the email address to receive it at. Does my registered company need to disclose who actually owns and controls it, beyond just the listed directors?

Yes — under the Companies Act, private companies must maintain and disclose a register of beneficial owners to BRS, separate from the directors listed on your CR12. A beneficial owner is anyone holding at least 10% of shares or voting rights (directly or indirectly), anyone with the right to appoint or remove directors, or anyone who otherwise exercises significant influence or control over the company. What is Turnover Tax and who has to pay it?

Turnover Tax (TOT) applies to businesses with gross turnover of more than KES 1,000,000 but not exceeding KES 25,000,000 in a year of income. It does not apply to non-residents, and an eligible person can opt out by giving written notice to the KRA Commissioner. If your business earns below KES 1,000,000 a year you are exempt from TOT, though you still need to declare and file a corporate/income tax return. How do I know if a lender offering me a business loan is actually regulated, and why does that matter?

Check whether the lender is licensed by the Central Bank of Kenya — CBK licenses and regularly inspects commercial banks, microfinance banks, and other financial institutions to ensure they comply with the Banking Act, the Microfinance Act, and CBK's Prudential Guidelines. Licensed lenders must also submit your credit data to Credit Reference Bureaus monthly, building a verifiable credit history, whereas an unlicensed lender offers none of that oversight, credit reporting, or regulatory recourse if something goes wrong. Is BRS the only official record of registered businesses in Kenya?

Yes — BRS describes itself as the sole custodian of the list of companies and information for entities registered in Kenya, meaning it is the authoritative register other institutions (like banks or the tax authority) rely on to confirm a business is genuinely registered. If you need to prove your business is registered, an Official Search through BRS is the way to confirm what is on that record. How much does it cost to register a business name in Kenya?

Registering a business name through the Business Registration Service costs KES 950, paid online as part of the application on brsv2.ecitizen.go.ke. This is a single payment covering the name search and registration together — there is no separate name-reservation fee under the current BRS V2 process. This keeps your BRS record accurate, which matters if a bank, county government, or supplier ever verifies your registration details.
